**The document does not report HumanEval pass@1 retention for Qwen3 14B→32B or any other pair.** HumanEval is not among the benchmarks the paper evaluates.

The paper evaluates these benchmarks:

- **Main benchmarks:** ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, MMLU 5-shot, GSM8K 8-shot with chain-of-thought, and WikiText-2 perplexity. CoQA is used for multi-turn handoff (p. 6; Table 11, p. 16).
- **Generation benchmark:** GSM8K is the only one in Table 11 (p. 16).
- **Held-out benchmarks:** PIQA, BoolQ and ARC-Easy (Table 18, p. 21).
- **Calibration-domain sweep:** ARC-Easy, PIQA and BoolQ alongside the main benchmarks (Table 9, p. 16).

The closest available results for Qwen3 14B→32B with ridge at k=8 are:

- **Average retention across the five main benchmarks:** 97.6%. Per benchmark, it is 101.0% on ARC-C, 97.6% on HellaSwag, 98.5% on WinoGrande, 95.0% on MMLU and 95.6% on GSM8K (Table 1, p. 6).
- **Held-out retention:** 98.0% on PIQA, 101.9% on BoolQ and 99.8% on ARC-Easy (Table 18, p. 21).

Calibration used one code-related dataset: CodeAlpaca was tested as an alternative calibration corpus (Tables 8–9, pp. 15–16). That was not a code-generation evaluation, so it says nothing about HumanEval performance.
